name: Charles Darwin
desc: Originator of the theory of evolution by natural selection. Author of On the Origin of Species (1859). Also worked on sexual selection, earthworms, coral reefs, and plant domestication.
contributions: Natural Selection;On the Origin of Species;Sexual selection;Coral reef theory

name: AR Wallace
desc: Co-discoverer of evolution by natural selection with Darwin. Famous for field work in SE Asia. Father of biogeography — Wallace's line separating Asian and Australasian fauna.

name: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
desc: Pre-Darwin French evolutionary theory, believed in inheritance of acquired characteristics. Also an influential invertebrate taxonomist, may have coined the term invertebrate.

name: Georges Cuvier
desc: Father of paleontology. Showed that extinction occurred, championed catastrophism. Established comparative anatomy and stratigraphy. Described pterodactyl, mosasaur, mastodon. Opposed evolution.

name: Comte de Buffon
desc: 1700s French naturalist, predecessor of Lamarck. Early precursor to evolutionary ideas. Argued the world was 75000 years old, much older than previously thought.

name: Charles Lyell
desc: 19th century British geologist whose ideas about gradualism were perhaps the greatest influence on Darwin's thinking about deep time.

name: Thomas Huxley
desc: Darwin's bulldog, champion of his ideas in public debate and scientific circles.

name: Ernst Haeckel
desc: 19th century German evolutionary biologist and champion of Darwin. Famous for Art Forms in Nature and the concept that ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny.
contributions: Ontogeny recapitulates phylogeny;Art forms in nature

name: Richard Owen
desc: Key 1800s British anatomist, opponent of Darwin. Coined the term dinosaur. Believed species were independent creations.

name: Gregor Mendel
desc: Founder of classical genetics through pea plant experiments. Discovered laws of segregation and independent assortment. His work was unrecognized until 1900.

name: Hugo de Vries
desc: Dutch botanist and very early geneticist. Independently rediscovered Mendel's work. Coined term mutation in genetics. Advocated for Mutationism — evolution by large-scale mutations.

name: Moritz Wagner
desc: Early 19th century German naturalist, believer in the primary importance of geological isolation in speciation, leading to conflict with Darwin.

name: David Starr Jordan
desc: Influential ichthyologist and 1st president of Stanford. Championed geographic isolation in speciation. Also a hardcore eugenicist.

name: Karl Jordan
desc: Turn-of-the-century entomologist later championed by Mayr, credited with originating the Biological Species Concept.

name: Joseph Grinnell
desc: Founder of the Museum of Vertebrate Zoology (MVZ) at Berkeley. Conducted extensive surveys of birds and mammals of California.

name: Frank Chapman
desc: AMNH curator of birds. Founded the Christmas Bird Count. Pioneering birder and ornithologist in North and South America.

name: Louis Vieillot
desc: Early French ornithologist who described Quiscalus major in 1819 and genus Quiscalus in 1816.

name: JF Gmelin
desc: Early German naturalist who described Quiscalus mexicanus in 1788.

name: William Bateson
desc: Very early geneticist: first to use the term genetics. Advocate for Mendel's work. Co-discovered linkage with Punnett and Saunders. Proposed Dobzhansky-Muller model before they did.

name: Reginald Punnett
desc: Early geneticist working with Bateson. Co-discovered genetic linkage. Best known for the Punnett square.

name: Edith Saunders
desc: Mother of English plant genetics. Co-discovered linkage with Bateson and Punnett. With Bateson coined alleomorph (allele). Worked on flower anatomy.

name: Hardy and Weinberg
desc: English mathematician GH Hardy and German physician Wilhelm Weinberg independently proposed Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium in 1908, foundational to population genetics.

name: William E. Castle
desc: Harvard geneticist who worked on coat color genetics in mammals. PhD advisor of Sewell Wright.
contributions: Mammalian coat color genetics;Population genetics precursor

name: TH Morgan
desc: Nobel laureate who established that genes are carried on chromosomes and discovered sex-linked inheritance. Dobzhansky worked in his lab.
contributions: Chromosomal theory of inheritance;Sex-linked traits;Nobel Prize

name: RA Fisher
desc: One of the great triumvirate of Modern Synthesis population geneticists. Foundational for statistics and evolution: ANOVA, p=0.05 threshold, Wright-Fisher model, Fisherian runaway, Fisher's principle for sex ratios, maximum likelihood. Also a eugenicist and racist.
contributions: ANOVA;p=0.05 threshold;Fisherian runaway;Fisher's principle (sex ratio);Maximum likelihood;Wright-Fisher model

name: Sewell Wright
desc: Part of the great triumvirate. Pioneered inbreeding coefficient, F-statistics, genetic drift, Wright-Fisher model, and the adaptive landscape/fitness peaks metaphor. Contra Fisher, believed genetic drift could be a strong evolutionary force.

name: JBS Haldane
desc: Part of the great triumvirate. Haldane's rule on hybrid sterility, heterozygote advantage (malaria/sickle cell), and abiogenesis in primordial soup. John Maynard Smith was a student.

name: Barbara McClintock
desc: Discoverer of transposable elements. First to demonstrate crossing over in meiosis. Won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

name: Watson and Crick
desc: Determined the structure of DNA (double helix) in 1953, using X-ray crystallography data largely from Rosalind Franklin without her explicit consent.

name: Rosalind Franklin
desc: Produced the X-ray crystallography data critical to determining DNA's structure. Her contribution was largely uncredited by Watson and Crick at the time.

name: Frederick Sanger
desc: Developed chain-termination (dideoxy) DNA sequencing in 1977; the original method used radioactive labels, with fluorescent dyes added later by others. Won two Nobel Prizes in Chemistry, one for protein sequencing (insulin) and one for DNA sequencing.

name: Kary Mullis
desc: Inventor of PCR (polymerase chain reaction), a transformative tool for molecular biology. Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1993. An eccentric figure.

name: Ernst Mayr
desc: Central figure in the modern synthesis. Worked with New Guinea birds. Championed allopatric speciation and invented the Biological Species Concept (BSC).

name: Theodosius Dobzhansky
desc: Central figure in the modern synthesis. Key to understanding reproductive isolation as central to speciation. Worked mostly with Drosophila, including under TH Morgan.
contributions: Reproductive isolation;Genetics and Origin of Species;Drosophila genetics;Dobzhansky-Muller model

name: George Stebbins
desc: The most important botanist in developing the modern synthesis. Harvard PhD, Berkeley then Davis professor. Wrote about polyploidy for speciation in plants.
contributions: Polyploidy and speciation;Plant evolutionary biology;Variation and Evolution in Plants

name: John Maynard Smith
desc: Student of Haldane. Pioneered evolutionary game theory (ESS). Also important contributions to kin selection and the evolution of sex.

name: Jurgen Haffer
desc: Originator of the Pleistocene refugia theory to explain Amazon biodiversity — that forest refugia during ice ages drove speciation of Amazonian birds.

name: Jon Fjeldsa
desc: Danish ornithologist working on Andes birds and speciation patterns in South America and Africa.

name: James Crow
desc: Distinguished population geneticist at Wisconsin. Advisor of Motoo Kimura. Key work on mutation rates, genetic load, and population genetics theory.

name: Motoo Kimura
desc: Founder of the neutral theory of molecular evolution. Student of James Crow. Advisor of Tomoko Ohta. Developed infinite alleles and infinite sites models.
contributions: Neutral theory;Diffusion approximations;Infinite alleles model;Infinite sites model

name: Tomoko Ohta
desc: Founder of nearly neutral theory — an extension of Kimura's neutral theory incorporating slightly deleterious mutations.

name: Masatoshi Nei
desc: Population geneticist. Developed neighbor-joining methods for phylogenies and Nei's genetic distance.

name: Richard Lewontin
desc: Harvard population geneticist. Coined linkage disequilibrium. Protein electrophoresis work measured high genetic variation. Spandrels with Gould. Student of Dobzhansky, advisor of Felsenstein and Coyne.
contributions: Linkage disequilibrium;Protein electrophoresis;Spandrels (with Gould);Critique of adaptationism

name: Stephen Jay Gould
desc: Harvard paleontologist and prolific science popularizer. Punctuated equilibrium with Eldredge. Spandrels critique of adaptationism with Lewontin. Opposed sociobiology and evolutionary psychology.

name: Joe Felsenstein
desc: Widely revered theoretician of molecular phylogenetics. Maximum likelihood for phylogenies, bootstrapping, PHYLIP software, phylogenetic comparative methods, Santa Rosalia paper, anomaly zone, tree-pruning algorithm.
contributions: Maximum likelihood phylogenetics;Bootstrapping;PHYLIP;Phylogenetic comparative methods;Santa Rosalia paper

name: Allan Wilson
desc: Berkeley molecular evolutionist who pioneered use of molecular clocks. Work on mitochondrial DNA and human origins. Advisor of Scott Edwards.

name: John Avise
desc: Founder of phylogeography using mtDNA. Early adopter of allozymes and later mtDNA for studying genetic variation across geography.
contributions: Phylogeography;mtDNA in systematics;Allozymes in population genetics

name: Monty Slatkin
desc: Berkeley population genetics theoretician. Advisor of Scott Edwards, John Wakeley, and Mark Kirkpatrick.
contributions: Gene flow theory;Ancient DNA methods;Population subdivision

name: Nick Barton
desc: Theoretical population geneticist. Work on hybrid zones, barriers to gene flow, and linked selection. Postdoctoral advisor of Sarah Otto.
contributions: Hybrid zone theory;Linked selection;Barriers to gene flow

name: Marcus Feldman
desc: Stanford theoretician. Modifier theory for the evolution of recombination, and cultural evolution with Cavalli-Sforza. PhD advisor of Sarah Otto.

name: EO Wilson
desc: Harvard professor and famous ant researcher. With MacArthur developed theory of island biogeography. Conducted fumigation experiments with Simberloff. Wrote on kin selection and Sociobiology.
contributions: Island biogeography theory;Sociobiology;Kin selection;Character displacement;Ant ecology

name: G. Evelyn Hutchinson
desc: Father of modern ecology. Yale professor who trained MacArthur. Seminal Santa Rosalia paper on coexistence. Defined the n-dimensional hypervolume niche concept.

name: Robert MacArthur
desc: With EO Wilson developed theory of island biogeography. Famous work on niche partitioning in warblers. Student of G. Evelyn Hutchinson at Yale.

name: Mary Jane West-Eberhard
desc: Key thinker on sexual selection, phenotypic plasticity, and developmental plasticity in evolution.

name: Peter and Rosemary Grant
desc: Famous researchers of Darwin's finches in the Galapagos. Princeton professors. Long-term study of natural selection in action is a landmark of evolutionary field biology.

name: Robert Selander
desc: Penn State ornithologist. Did the most extensive work on the biology and sympatry of grackles.

name: Van Remsen
desc: Longtime LSU Curator of Birds, highly influential neotropical ornithologist. Too many students to name.

name: Ned Johnson
desc: Famed Berkeley bird curator. Extensive work on bird systematics and field biology. Advisor of Scott Edwards and Bob Zink, among others.

name: Jim Patton
desc: Famed Berkeley mammologist and curator, working mostly on systematics of small mammals. Extensive fieldwork in South America.

name: Joel Cracraft
desc: AMNH curator and influential ornithologist. Champion of the phylogenetic species concept.

name: Herb Dessauer
desc: Louisiana herpetologist at LSU medical center. Founder of the LSUMNS tissue collection. Very early work on molecular systematics of Anolis.

name: George Lowery
desc: LSUMNS founder. Described Quiscalus mexicanus prosopidicola in 1938. Also has Q. m. loweryi named after him.

name: Fran James
desc: LSU graduate student who became first female president of the American Ornithological Society. Studied Red-winged Blackbird dispersal.

name: Stevenson
desc: Florida ornithologist who described eye color variation in Boat-tailed Grackle (BTGR), including describing the new subspecies alabamensis.

name: Scott Edwards
desc: Harvard curator of birds. Worked extensively on coalescent theory and gene tree discordance in ornithology. Student of Ned Johnson, Monty Slatkin, Allan Wilson.

name: Hopi Hoekstra
desc: Harvard mammalologist. Worked on MC1R and experimental evolution of coat color in Peromyscus mice, connecting genotype to phenotype to ecology.
contributions: MC1R and coat color;Peromyscus evolution;Genotype-phenotype mapping

name: Robb Brumfield
desc: LSU Curator of Birds. PhD with Michael Braun at U Maryland. Works on systematics and evolution of Neotropical birds, including hybrid zone studies.

name: Matthew Hahn
desc: Population geneticist at Indiana. Cruickshank and Hahn on Fst vs. Dxy. Proponent of linked selection. Author of population genetics textbook.
contributions: Fst vs. Dxy debate;Linked selection;Population genetics textbook

name: Sarah Otto
desc: UBC professor working on theory and modeling. Genome size evolution, sexual vs. asexual organisms, experiments in yeast. Stanford PhD; postdoctoral advisor was Nick Barton.
contributions: Genome size evolution;Sexual vs. asexual;Yeast experimental evolution

name: Mohammad Noor
desc: Duke professor, UChicago PhD (student of Coyne). Works on chromosomal inversions, recombination rate, lethal alleles in Drosophila, reinforcement, and speciation genetics.

name: H. Allen Orr
desc: University of Rochester professor. Drosophila geneticist and co-author with Coyne of Speciation. Studies reproductive isolation and the genetics of adaptation.

name: Jerry Coyne
desc: Drosophila researcher and co-author with Orr of Speciation. Student of Lewontin at Harvard.

name: Trevor Price
desc: UChicago professor and author of Speciation in Birds. Student of Peter Grant. Worked on Greenish warbler ring species and character displacement.
contributions: Speciation in Birds;Greenish warbler ring species;Character displacement

name: Dolph Schluter
desc: UBC professor. Works with sticklebacks. Adaptive radiations, parallel evolution, ecological speciation. Student of Peter Grant.

name: Jim Mallet
desc: Harvard professor working with Heliconius butterflies on speciation and hybridization. Proponent of genetic cluster species concept.
contributions: Heliconius hybridization;Genetic cluster species concept;Speciation theory

name: Rebecca Safran
desc: Colorado Boulder professor (Cornell PhD). Works on sexual selection and speciation in Barn Swallows.

name: Robert Zink
desc: Emeritus curator at Minnesota. PhD from UC Berkeley with Ned Johnson. Molecular systematist, critic of glacial refugia paradigm. Brewster medal.

name: Daniel Simberloff
desc: Ecologist at U Tennessee. EO Wilson's student. Did island fumigation experiments with Wilson. Works on biological invasions and metapopulations.

name: Bob Ricklefs
desc: Ornithologist and ecologist. Student of MacArthur. Life history tradeoffs, taxon cycles on islands.
contributions: Life history tradeoffs;Island taxon cycles;Growth rate evolution

name: Wayne Maddison
desc: UBC professor who developed MacClade and Mesquite software for phylogenetic analysis. Works on jumping spiders.

name: Brant Faircloth
desc: LSU professor (Georgia PhD with John Carroll). Influential work on phylogenetics using ultra-conserved elements (UCEs).

name: Michael Hellberg
desc: LSU professor. PhD with Richard Grosberg at UC Davis. Works on speciation and genetics of corals and other marine animals.
contributions: Coral genetics;Marine population genetics;Gene flow in marine systems

name: Gary Graves
desc: Smithsonian curator of birds, former LSU PhD student. Variety of work on birds, including in the Andes.

name: Jared Diamond
desc: Ornithologist who worked on New Guinea birds. Also influential writer outside ornithology: Guns Germs and Steel.
contributions: New Guinea birds;Ethnobiology of species concepts;Guns Germs Steel
